title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer during regional failover and tighten backoff hysteresis
author: Marcus Li
description:
Summary: This hotfix addresses a production incident where the SLO enforcer would thrash during multi-region failover and trigger excessive load-shedding. Root cause: an ordering/race between region health transitions and the backoff/hysteresis window that caused the enforcer to flip states rapidly (open/close circuit) and evict healthy in-flight requests. Impact: elevated 99th percentile latency and increased error budget burn during an AWS region failover test.

What I changed: 1) Fix ordering race in regional transition path by making health transition operations idempotent and serializing the state change path with a lightweight compare-and-swap documented in code comments. 2) Tighten default backoff/hysteresis logic: introduce a configurable hysteresis multiplier and minimum backoff window to prevent sub-second flips. 3) Add quorum-based failover gating so a single transient health signal from control plane does not immediately trigger cross-region circuit opens. 4) Improve load-shedding policy to prefer degraded routing (slower model variant / lower batch size) before hard shedding. 5) Add metrics and tracing hooks: enforcer_state_transitions, backoff_window_seconds, failover_quorum_status to make postmortems and alerts actionable. 6) Add unit and integration tests that simulate rapid region flaps, and a small canary job in perf-canary to exercise the change. 7) Add an emergency rollout config (feature flag) to tighten hysteresis further for affected tenants.

Testing: Unit tests added for state machine transitions and hysteresis boundaries. Integration test simulates 3-region topology with synthetic health signals. Perf canary ran against staging and showed no regression in median latency and eliminated flip behavior in 99th percentile under failover injection. CI initially flaked on an unrelated test (batch_scheduler_test) which was rerun and passed.

Rollout plan: cherry-pick to release/2026-02 for immediate affected clusters, staged rollout to Dedicated and Hosted backends over 48 hours. Monitor enforcer_state_transitions and SLO breach alerts; rollback plan via feature flag and immediate revert if error rates increase.

References: ENG-6784 (regional failover postmortem), SUP-4122 (support ticket from enterprise customer), previous related PRs pr-33102 and pr-30511 for SLO enforcer stabilization work.

Notes: This change is non-breaking and behind a feature flag; operators can revert hysteresis changes remotely. Code comments explain the compare-and-swap ordering semantics and testing harness for failover scenarios.
